newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds rise on Treasuries' heels.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds rise on Treasuries' heels.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities were higher late afternoon on Tuesday, having advanced in line with Treasuries after the release of a lower-than-expected index of business conditions in the nation's manufacturing sector.

The National Association of Purchasing Management's (NAPM) September index read 51.7, a few notches below economists' average forecast of 52.5. The index read 52.6 in August. A reading above 50 points signals expansion, while a reading below 50 signals a contraction.
In particular, agency pass-throughs were bolstered by heavy trading earlier in the day, according to traders.
"There's been some pretty good street-buying in mortgages today. I think (the market) is deal driven," said one New York-based trader.
Another trader noted that reported comments made by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan to Australia's Treasurer Peter Costello helped lift mortgage-backed prices.
According to a report by Financial Review, an Internet publication, Greenspan said that inflation is not an immediate risk in the United States and there is no need to raise rates.
By late afternoon, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent coupons were up 12/32 at 99-04/32, yielding 108 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent pass-throughs and Freddie Mac 30-years were both up 12/32 to 99-07/32 and 99-11/32, respectively.
The 10-year note was up 14/32 to yield 6.64 in late trading.
